institution: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow
citation: Department of Microbiology, Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, Lucknow. News Letter, Issue 5 (published March 2018): antibiograms for antibiotics and antifungals, January to December 2017. Lucknow: Dr. RMLIMS; 2018.
reporting: Percent susceptible with the number of isolates, by specimen (blood, body fluids, urine, respiratory, pus) and organism, each row one location (ICU, OPD, IPD or SRCLI) shown by the row colour; organism isolation bar charts (with printed data labels) per specimen and location.
method: AST method and breakpoint edition not stated for the tables; the report's MRSA note (p24) says cefoxitin disc testing is the surrogate for methicillin resistance.

verification.note: Tables (PDF pages 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 14): cell text parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (ruled table cells; rotated organism labels matched to rows by position) and the location of each row from its background colour sampled on the page rendered at scale 3 (legend: ICU grey, OPD salmon, IPD yellow, SRCLI blue). Every cell was then compared with the rendered page by overlaying the parsed text on the page image (scale 3, one crop per table section): no differences. Organism charts (pages 6, 9 and 12) are vector graphics: each bar was matched to its legend entry by identical fill colour (bar order equals legend order in every box) and to its data label by position, and all 20 boxes were compared with the page images. The chart counts add up to each box's culture-positive total (for example blood OPD 67, blood IPD 209), which is how the rows with contradicted locations (see notes and excluded) were identified. Page numbers are PDF page numbers (the printed page number is one lower).

notes: Dr. RMLIMS Lucknow Microbiology News Letter, Issue 5 (March 2018), antibiograms for antibiotics and antifungals, January to December 2017. Each specimen table has one row per organism and location, the location shown only by the row colour: ICU, OPD, IPD (recorded as wards) and SRCLI (State Referral Centre for Laboratory Investigation, a separate location category, not recorded). Specimens: blood; body fluids (recorded as sterile body fluids); urine; respiratory specimens (sputum, BAL, mini BAL, throat swab and tracheal aspirate); pus. Organisms are printed at genus level in the blood and urine tables (Enterococcus, Citrobacter, Enterobacter, Klebsiella, Proteus, Acinetobacter and Pseudomonas spp.) and at species level in the other tables; "Pseudomonas spp." is recorded under the P. aeruginosa key. Rows are recorded as printed, including rows of 1 to 5 isolates (the report applies no minimum). The blood table has a single HLG/G column (high-level gentamicin for enterococci, gentamicin for staphylococci). Where the organism charts and the tables disagree on which location a row belongs to, the rows are not recorded (see excluded): the blood Enterococcus spp., CoNS and S. aureus OPD and IPD rows (the table colours give OPD n=15, 94, 15 and IPD n=5, 32, 8; the charts give OPD 5, 32, 8 and IPD 15, 94, 15, and the chart totals match each box), the body-fluid A. baumannii OPD and IPD rows (table OPD 1, IPD 8; chart OPD 8, IPD 1) and the pus E. coli OPD row (the row coloured OPD has n=55 and the one coloured SRCLI n=137; the chart gives OPD 137, SRCLI 55). Other chart and table disagreements are noted on the rows (blood IPD Enterobacter 14 against 40; respiratory ICU P. mirabilis 11 against 10 and no P. aeruginosa bar against 85 in the table; pus OPD E. faecalis 12 against 9). Counts are the ICU, IPD and OPD chart labels, including Candida spp. in blood and urine. The antifungal table prints numbers of isolates, not percentages, and is not recorded. The live URL returns 404; the PDF was downloaded from the Internet Archive copy of the same URL.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell re-read from the page images (tables pp7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 14 at scale 3 to 4, header row attached to each crop) and typed out before comparing with the file: all 2,304 cells (the seeded sample of 576 from sample_cells.py is part of this), all 139 row n and all 139 row locations. 0 transcription errors, no value changed. A third, mechanical read (text-layer characters assigned to colour bands and header columns) agrees on all 2,304 numbers; its one oddity is a stray large "7" in the text layer at body-fluid OPD P. aeruginosa netilmicin, which the page shows as 72 (recorded 72).

Second reader: locations checked by eye and by sampling each row's fill colour against the page legend (ICU grey, OPD salmon, IPD yellow, SRCLI blue; the body-fluid IPD rows use a stronger yellow). Row order differs between tables (blood ICU, OPD, IPD, SRCLI; urine, respiratory and pus ICU, IPD, OPD, SRCLI; pus E. coli ICU, IPD, SRCLI, OPD), so it cannot stand in for the colour; every recorded row carries the location of its colour.

Second reader: all 172 counts re-read from the organism charts (pp6, 9, 12; each bar matched to its legend entry by colour and order): all as recorded. The three count mismatches are printed that way (source inconsistencies): blood IPD Enterobacter spp. chart 14, table 40; respiratory ICU P. mirabilis chart 11, table 10; pus OPD E. faecalis chart 12, table 9.

Second reader: the 9 rows excluded for a contradicted location are right. The charts give the OPD and IPD numbers the other way round from the table colours for blood Enterococcus spp. (chart OPD 5, IPD 15; table 15, 5), CoNS (32, 94; table 94, 32), S. aureus (8, 15; table 15, 8) and body-fluid A. baumannii (8, 1; table 1, 8), and pus E. coli OPD 137, SRCLI 55 against the OPD-coloured row 55 and the SRCLI-coloured row 137. The charts are the self-consistent side (the blood OPD box has 67 culture positives in all, so it cannot hold 94 CoNS, and the blood ICU and SRCLI GPC rows agree with their charts), so the blood GPC OPD and IPD row colours look swapped; the rows stay out because the source contradicts itself.

Second reader: every cell the validator does not keep is printed as recorded: 36 caution cells (24 findings in 21 rows: 9 tetracycline above doxycycline, 3 imipenem against meropenem, 8 colistin 0 to 40%, blood ICU S. aureus linezolid 83, and blood ICU Enterococcus chloramphenicol 92 of 11, blood OPD Klebsiella cefepime 5 of 4 and urine IPD Enterobacter nitrofurantoin 35 of 8, which no whole number of isolates gives), the 7 suppressed staphylococcal cefoperazone-sulbactam cells (36, 33, 100, 91, 14, 68 and 50, each above cefoxitin) and all 149 intrinsic cells.

Second reader: urine Klebsiella spp. (p10). In all four rows (ICU 6, IPD 6, OPD 16 and the unrecorded SRCLI 23) the page prints the numbers centred in the COL and OFFLOX cells (colistin 0, 0, 15, 65; ofloxacin 0, 20, 7, 64) and "-" in the TOB, NX and NF cells, and the text layer places them at the COL and OFFLOX header centres. The E. coli, Citrobacter, Enterobacter and Acinetobacter rows show the reverse (values under TOB, NX and NF, "-" under COL and OFFLOX) and the Proteus spp. rows print values under COL only, so a one-column shift in the source is possible, but nothing on the page shows one: kept as printed with the extractor's notes.

Second reader: notes corrected, no values changed. The blood rows' HLG/G note said every other table prints GENTA and HLG separately, but the urine table has only an HLG column (high-level gentamicin in the report's abbreviation list), where its staphylococcal gentamicin figures sit; the four urine staphylococcal rows now say so. Added to excluded that the blood OPD organism chart counts 1 Citrobacter spp. where the table prints a 0-isolate OPD row.
